title: MambaVoiceCloning: Efficient and Expressive Text-to-Speech via State-Space Modeling and Diffusion Control
claim: A multi-stage system turns text and reference audio into speech through all-SSM conditioning, with a training-only aligner supervising it.
layout: Four colored stage blocks left-to-right, dashed loss feedback loops along the bottom
description: A wide block diagram split into four pastel rounded regions labeled Input Stage (cyan), Encoder Stage (mint), Speech Dynamics Stage (light green) and Decoder Stage (pink). Text tokens and a spectrogram waveform enter on the left. They pass through the Bi-Mamba Text Encoder, Text Aligner, Expressive Mamba Encoder, Pitch Extractor and Temporal Bi-Mamba Encoder. Solid black arrows then lead through Temporal, Expressive and Noise/Pitch predictors to a HiFi-GAN/iSTFTNet decoder. Along the bottom, the generated audio goes to a diffusion denoiser and then to the final waveform, and to discriminators. Dashed arrows carry alignment, temporal, adversarial and mel losses into a grey Training Loss parallelogram. The eye starts at the top-left red text input and follows the arrows rightward. Saturated box fills make the modules stand out.
caption: Overview of MambaVoiceCloning (MVC). The framework uses Bi-Mamba Text Encoders for phoneme modeling, a Temporal Bi-Mamba for rhythmic alignment, and an Expressive Mamba for prosodic control. A lightweight aligner (dotted box) provides phoneme--frame supervision only during training, ensuring an SSM-only encoder at inference. Conditioning features drive a diffusion decoder and vocoder for waveform synthesis.
abstract: MambaVoiceCloning (MVC) asks whether the conditioning path of diffusion-based TTS can be made fully SSM-only at inference, removing all attention and explicit RNN-style recurrence layers across text, rhythm, and prosody, while preserving or improving quality under controlled conditions. MVC combines a gated bidirectional Mamba text encoder, a Temporal Bi-Mamba supervised by a lightweight alignment teacher discarded after training, and an Expressive Mamba with AdaLN modulation, yielding linear-time O(T) conditioning with bounded activation memory and practical finite look-ahead streaming. Unlike prior Mamba-TTS systems that remain hybrid at inference, MVC removes attention-based duration and style modules under a fixed StyleTTS2 mel-diffusion-vocoder backbone. Trained on LJSpeech/LibriTTS and evaluated on VCTK, CSS10 (ES/DE/FR), and long-form Gutenberg passages, MVC achieves modest but statistically reliable gains over StyleTTS2, VITS, and Mamba-attention hybrids in MOS/CMOS, F0 RMSE, MCD, and WER, while reducing encoder parameters to 21M and improving throughput by 1.6x. Diffusion remains the dominant latency source, but SSM-only conditioning improves memory footprint, stability, and deployability.
